headline: Measurement is comparison against a standard—turning the qualitative into the quantitative
universal_truth: What gets measured gets managed; precision enables progress
fun_facts: The meter was originally defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the equator to the North Pole
Ancient measurements were based on body parts—the 'foot', the 'cubit' (forearm length)
The kilogram was redefined in 2019—it's now based on a quantum physics constant, not a physical object
discussion_questions: What would be hard to do without standard measurements?
Why did different cultures develop different measurement systems?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: How tall is that building? How heavy is this package? How hot is the oven? Measurement answers these questions by comparing unknown quantities to agreed-upon standards. It's how we turn 'pretty big' into 'exactly 4.7 meters.'

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Measurement seems obvious—just use a ruler. But where do standards come from? Why is a meter a meter? Who decided, and why does everyone agree?
cliff.prompt: How do measurement standards get established?

options.text: By international agreement, choosing definitions that are stable, reproducible, and universal
options.response: Yes. Modern standards are based on unchanging physical constants, ensuring everyone's meter is identical.

options.text: Powerful countries imposed their systems on others
options.response: Historically some systems spread through power, but today we seek universal physics-based standards...

q1.title: Body-Based Origins
q1.script: Early measurements used what was available: body parts. A 'foot' was literally a foot. A 'cubit' was elbow to fingertip. The problem? Everyone's body differs. Trade and construction needed something more consistent.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Body-Based Origins"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Metric Revolution
q2.script: The metric system, born from the French Revolution, aimed for universal standards based on nature, not kings. One meter was defined as one ten-millionth of the Earth's quadrant. Rational, consistent, and—eventually—global.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Beyond Objects
q3.script: Modern standards don't rely on physical objects—which can change. Since 2019, the kilogram is defined by Planck's constant, a value from quantum physics that never varies. Our measurements are now anchored in the fabric of reality.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What gets measured gets managed. Measurement enables precision, and precision enables progress. Vague terms hide confusion. When something matters, find a way to measure it.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 104. Tomorrow, we'll explore the math of shapes—geometry. Until then, appreciate that your ruler carries millennia of human effort to agree on standards.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Measurement Appreciation - Notice the Standards
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate the measurement systems around you
growTrack.activity: Notice measurements today: temperatures, distances, weights, volumes. Each relies on an agreed standard. Consider: what if these standards didn't exist? What would be different about your day?
